svg.title: Compare Retention, Not Passenger Fare Volume
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-subniche-retained-yield-bars; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Compare Retention, Not Passenger Fare Volume; subtitle: Five illustrative sub-niches measured as retained dollars per $100 of operator billings.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Each bar represents $100 of gross operator billings before operator overhead. Equal billing weights across yields of $60, $50, $65, $45, and $55 produce the canonical 55% blended retained share. These are illustrative contract economics, not observed market yields or separate scorecard forecasts.; caption: Collection rails affect settlement speed, fees, and reversals; they do not create the underlying yield. Maintain separate contract, payment-fee, and failed-collection fields. The canonical scenarios retain 55% regardless of this illustrative niche mix.; stages: label: Weekly rideshare driver leases; value: $60 retained per $100 billed through authorized ACH collections; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Illustrative $40 owner and pass-through allocation leaves $60 before operator overhead. Reconcile scheduled lease collections to cleared cash; an ACH initiation does not establish final payment.; label: Licensed Black SUV shift dispatch; value: $50 retained per $100 billed through reconciled commercial settlements; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Illustrative $50 owner and vehicle-service allocation leaves $50 before overhead. Measure operator dispatch billings rather than all passenger fares; airport waiting and empty repositioning can destroy shift contribution.; label: Investor vehicle co-hosting; value: $65 retained per $100 of gross co-hosting billings; numeric value: 65.0; detail: Illustrative $35 contractually payable owner and pass-through allocation leaves $65. Where the operator bills only a management fee in practice, reassess the billing denominator instead of importing investor receipts.; label: Short-duration replacement vehicles; value: $45 retained per $100 billed through documented short-term rentals; numeric value: 45.0; detail: Illustrative $55 owner and pass-through allocation leaves $45 before overhead. Delivery labor, cleaning, charge reversals, and idle days require separate tracking; deposits remain liabilities until properly applied.; label: Commercial sedan driver leases; value: $55 retained per $100 billed through scheduled business collections; numeric value: 55.0; detail: Illustrative $45 owner and pass-through allocation matches the canonical blend. Attach toll evidence to each permitted charge and distinguish recurring rent from reimbursements and separately disclosed administration fees.

rect.title: label: Weekly rideshare driver leases; value: $60 retained per $100 billed through authorized ACH collections; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Illustrative $40 owner and pass-through allocation leaves $60 before operator overhead. Reconcile scheduled lease collections to cleared cash; an ACH initiation does not establish final payment.

label: Licensed Black SUV shift dispatch; value: $50 retained per $100 billed through reconciled commercial settlements; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Illustrative $50 owner and vehicle-service allocation leaves $50 before overhead. Measure operator dispatch billings rather than all passenger fares; airport waiting and empty repositioning can destroy shift contribution.

label: Investor vehicle co-hosting; value: $65 retained per $100 of gross co-hosting billings; numeric value: 65.0; detail: Illustrative $35 contractually payable owner and pass-through allocation leaves $65. Where the operator bills only a management fee in practice, reassess the billing denominator instead of importing investor receipts.

label: Short-duration replacement vehicles; value: $45 retained per $100 billed through documented short-term rentals; numeric value: 45.0; detail: Illustrative $55 owner and pass-through allocation leaves $45 before overhead. Delivery labor, cleaning, charge reversals, and idle days require separate tracking; deposits remain liabilities until properly applied.

label: Commercial sedan driver leases; value: $55 retained per $100 billed through scheduled business collections; numeric value: 55.0; detail: Illustrative $45 owner and pass-through allocation matches the canonical blend. Attach toll evidence to each permitted charge and distinguish recurring rent from reimbursements and separately disclosed administration fees.

text.title: Assumptions: Each bar represents $100 of gross operator billings before operator overhead. Equal billing weights across yields of $60, $50, $65, $45, and $55 produce the canonical 55% blended retained share. These are illustrative contract economics, not observed market yields or separate scorecard forecasts.
